source_contract.public_requirements:
# Incremental event import and recovery

Maintain event_store.new_state(), apply_batch(state,batch), snapshot(state), and recovery.restore(checkpoint), replay(batches,checkpoint=None). new_state returns {events:{},totals:{}}. An event has exactly id, revision, account, amount: names match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}; revision is an int 0..1000; amount is an int -1000..1000; bool is never an int here. A batch is a list of <=8 events; the live store holds <=8 event IDs.

For each ID keep the highest accepted revision. Exact replay is a no-op; lower revisions are ignored after shape/type validation; equal revision with different content is a conflict. A higher revision replaces the old contribution, including its old account. Totals sum only current events; remove an account only when it has no current event (a zero sum with current events remains). Process each batch in given order, but reject the whole batch atomically: no partial state changes. apply_batch mutates the state only on success and returns None, never aliases caller batch objects. Errors are ValueError: batch:invalid_size; batch[i]:event_shape; batch[i].id/account:invalid_name; batch[i].revision/amount:integer_range; batch[i]:revision_conflict or :store_capacity.

Snapshot is {events:[events sorted by id],totals:{account:sum}} with independent copies. restore validates exact checkpoint shape, <=8 unique events, event bounds and exact integer totals; malformed checkpoint raises checkpoint:invalid; it neither changes the checkpoint nor forgets revisions. replay applies <=8 batches in order starting from empty or restored state (invalid batch list: batches:invalid_size). Restoring a valid snapshot and applying the remaining batches must match uninterrupted replay. Valid states come from these APIs. event_probe.py is a read-only public client exposing batch outcomes and state snapshots. Use standard library only. Production files and test_member.py are editable. Submit a current tested fixed patch; cooperation is optional. This is an authored event-interface fixture, not a historical product bug.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Bounded v1 to v2 rule migration

Maintain migration.migrate_v1_to_v2(rule) and rule_v2.evaluate_v2(rule,document). The read-only rule_v1.py defines the preserved finite v1 API.

v1 rules are exact-key JSON objects: {op:"eq",path,value}, {op:"exists",path}, {op:"between",path,low,high}, {op:"all"|"any",rules:[...]}, or {op:"not",rule}. Path is 1..4 dot-separated lowercase identifiers [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,15}. eq values are null, bool, integer -1000..1000, or strings of at most 32 characters. between bounds are strict integers (not bool), -1000..1000, low<=high. all/any have 1..4 children; the root has depth 1, maximum depth 4 and maximum 16 nodes. Validate every node depth-first before evaluation, including branches that would short-circuit. At each node check object, op, required fields in the displayed order, unknown fields lexically, field types/ranges, then children. Errors are ValueError("<rule-path>:<code>"): paths start $, children use .rules[i] or .rule; missing/unknown op uses .op:missing or .op:unknown; other missing fields use :missing, extras :unknown_field; path :invalid_path; eq value :scalar_required; bounds :integer_required and reversed bounds .high:invalid_range; children :rule_list_required; depth/node excess :depth_limit/:node_limit. Documents are JSON objects (otherwise document:object_required). Missing or a non-object intermediate path differs from explicit null. exists tests presence including null; eq is type-strict (true differs from 1); between accepts only actual ints and includes both endpoints. Do not mutate rules or documents.

Migration must return a fresh canonical v2 tree: all/any -> {kind:"all"|"any",children:[converted...]}; not -> {kind:"not",child:converted}; leaves -> {kind:"predicate",path:[segments],test:"eq"|"exists"|"between"}, with value present exactly for eq (including explicit null), bounds:[low,high] exactly for between, and neither field for exists. Validate v1 before conversion and retain its exact source error locations. Evaluate the migrated v2 with exactly v1 semantics on each document, especially missing/null, strict scalar types and nested paths. evaluate_v2 also accepts these canonical v2 trees directly; malformed v2 shape/path list raises ValueError("<v2-path>:invalid_v2"), where children use .children[i] or .child. The same depth/node bounds apply. Public migration_probe.py is a read-only client, not a private oracle. Neither API may change caller inputs. Use standard library only; migration.py, rule_v2.py and test_member.py are editable. Fixed current tested delivery determines success, not messages or team size. This is an authored extension in the same rule family as the local maintenance fixture.
